Which research answers your question?

Start with a fire-safety need, then compare the fuels, hardware and conditions behind the investigations. Select up to three families to read side by side.

How is the research ranked?

Each investigation receives 3 points for a direct match to a research area, 1 for a related match, and 0 for background relevance. These classifications come from the objectives and research connections recorded in this catalogue.

The overall ranking adds the prevention, detection and suppression scores, with equal weight for each area (up to 9 points). Select a specific area to rank that topic alone (up to 3 points). Equal scores share a rank; alphabetical order only arranges tied entries. Searching keeps the ranks from the full catalogue.

This is a transparent reading-priority score. It measures the recorded relevance of a study, not fire severity, research quality or equipment performance. A specialised study may be the first choice for its topic even when its overall score is lower. Each card shows the calculation and links to its research references.
